questions.question: Who among the following freedom fighters wrote the poem 'Vande Mataram' in 1875?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following freedom fighters wrote the poem 'Vande Mataram' in 1875?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bankim Chandra Chatterjee.

Key Points

  • Vande Mataram is a Sanskrit poem written by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee.

    • Vande Mataram was first sung by Rabindranath Tagore in 1896.
    • It was adopted by the constituent assembly on 24th January 1950.
    • Jadhunath Bhattacharya composed the music of Vande Mataram.

Additional Information

  • Bipin Chandra Pal was one of the influencers of the Swadeshi movement along with Sri Aurobindo. 
    • He vehemently opposed the partition of Bengal by the British colonial government in December 1903.
    • He was born in Habiganj on 7 Nov 1858 and completed his studies at the University of Calcutta.
  • Rabindranath Tagore was a Bengali poet, writer, and painter.
    • He was honoured with the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.
    • He is the first non-European to receive the Nobel Prize for Literature.
    • Rabindranath Tagore got the Nobel Prize for his work Gitanjali.
  • Bhagat Singh was an Indian communist revolutionary whose two acts of spectacular brutality against the British in India and execution at the age of 23 made him a famous hero of the Indian independence movement.

questions.question: Who among the following was one of the leaders of the Santhal rebellion?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following was one of the leaders of the Santhal rebellion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sidhu Manjihi.

Key Points

  • Santhal Rebellion took place during Lord Dalhousie (1848-1856) tenure at Rajmahal hills (in Jharkhand) led by Sidhu Manjhi.
  • Santhal uprising took place during 1855-56.
  • The tyrannical British revenue system, usury practices, and the zamindari system in India made Santhal peoples annoyed, and two Santhal brothers Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu organized 10,000 Santhals and proclaimed a rebellion against the British.
  • The Santhals are the largest tribal group in India found in Jharkhand, WestBengal, and Odisha.
  • Santhal Rebellion:
    • It was a rebellion against both the British colonial authority and zamindars by the Santhal people.
    • Leaders: Sidhu, Kahnu, Chand, and Bhairav.
    • Location: Jharkhand.
    • The rebellion was suppressed and largely shadowed by other rebellions.
    • To quell rebellion British created Santhal Pargana and special laws were
      passed protecting them.

Additional Information

  • Britishers invited the Santhals to come and settle in Jharkhand promising land and economic amenities.
  • Thus Santhals from different states came to settle in today's Jharkhand.
  • Later zamindars dominated these areas as they collected taxes and lent money at very high rates which the people could not generally pay and their lands were forcibly taken.
  • This became the roots of the Santhal rebellion.
  • In a fierce encounter, Santhals were defeated as they were fighting with bows and arrows while Britishers had modern weapons.
  • Sidhu was caught in August 1855 and was hanged on a banyan tree at a place called Panchkathia.

questions.question: At which of the following jails was Khudiram Bose sent to the gallows?
questions.questionHtml: At which of the following jails was Khudiram Bose sent to the gallows?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Muzaffarpur.

Key Points

  • Shahid Khudiram Bose was the youngest revolutionary freedom fighter who opposed British Raj in India.
  • He was born on  3 December 1889, in the Midnapore district of  West Bengal.
  • Khudiram Bose was sent to Muzaffarpur Jail under the charge of conspiracy to kill the Chief Presidency Magistrate DH Kingsford of Muzaffarpur, also known as the Muzaffarpur Conspiracy.
  •  He was executed there on August 11, 1908, at the age of 18 years which made him the youngest martyr of the Indian Independence Movement.

Additional Information

  • Khudiram, along with Prafulla Chaki, attempted to assassinate a British judge, Magistrate Douglas Kingsford, by throwing bombs at the carriage, carriage they suspected the man was in but unfortunately, Magistrate Kingsford was seated in a different carriage, and the throwing of bombs resulted in the deaths of two British women.
  • At the time of his hanging, Khudiram was 18 years, 8 months, and 11 days.
  • Prafulla Chaki shot himself just before the arrest.

questions.question: Who among the following freedom fighters is known as 'Deshbandhu'?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following freedom fighters is known as 'Deshbandhu'?
questions.solution: Chittaranjan Das, popularly known as 'Deshbandhu' or 'Friend of the Nation,' was a distinguished freedom fighter and political leader. He played a pivotal role in the Non-Cooperation Movement and co-founded the Swaraj Party with Motilal Nehru to push for self-governance within the British Empire. A celebrated lawyer, Das famously defended Aurobindo Ghosh in the Alipore Bomb Case. An influential member of the Indian National Congress, he presided over its Gaya session in 1922 and significantly contributed to the strategies and policies of India's freedom struggle.

questions.question: In which of the following years was VD Savarkar sent to Andaman Jail by the British?
questions.questionHtml: In which of the following years was VD Savarkar sent to Andaman Jail by the British?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1911.

Key Points

  • Vinayak Damodar Savarkar, also known as Veer Savarkar, was a prominent freedom fighter, social reformer, and writer.
  • In 1910, Savarkar was arrested by the British for his involvement in revolutionary activities against the colonial regime.
  • He was subsequently tried and sentenced to two life terms of imprisonment totaling fifty years and was deported to the Andaman Islands in 1911.
  • The Cellular Jail in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, also known as Kala Pani, was where he was imprisoned. This jail was notorious for its harsh conditions and was used by the British to exile political prisoners.

Additional Information

  • Vinayak Damodar Savarkar:
    • He was born on May 28, 1883, in Bhagur, a village near Nashik in Maharashtra, India.
    • He was a staunch advocate of Hindutva and is credited with founding the ideology.
    • Savarkar wrote several books, including "The First War of Indian Independence 1857," which presented the uprising of 1857 as a unified and national effort against British rule.
    • After his release from prison, he continued his activities as a social reformer and political activist, although he was kept under strict surveillance by the British authorities.
  • Cellular Jail (Kala Pani):
    • The Cellular Jail is located in Port Blair, the capital of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
    • It was constructed by the British between 1896 and 1906 to exile political prisoners.
    • The jail is known for its solitary confinement cells, which were designed to isolate prisoners from each other and prevent them from communicating.
    • Many prominent Indian freedom fighters, including Batukeshwar Dutt, Yogendra Shukla, and more, were imprisoned here.
    • Today, the Cellular Jail is a national memorial monument.

questions.question: In 1936, The Independent Labour Party was founded by ______.
questions.questionHtml: In 1936, The Independent Labour Party was founded by ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is BR Ambedkar.

Key Points

  • Dr. BR Ambedkar was a prominent Indian jurist, economist, and social reformer who campaigned against social discrimination towards the untouchables (Dalits).
  • He was the principal architect of the Constitution of India and served as the first Law Minister of India.
  • In 1936, Dr. BR Ambedkar founded the Independent Labour Party, which aimed to secure social justice and eradicate social inequalities.
  • The party contested the Bombay Legislative Assembly elections held in 1937 and won 15 seats.

Additional Information

  • Independent Labour Party (ILP)
    • The Independent Labour Party was established by BR Ambedkar on 15 August 1936 in Bombay.
    • The ILP was formed to address the issues faced by the working class and the marginalized sections of society, particularly the Dalits.
    • The party's manifesto emphasized the need for state socialism in the sphere of industry and agriculture.
    • It also advocated for labor rights, including fair wages, decent working conditions, and social security measures for workers.
  • BR Ambedkar
    • Born on 14 April 1891, Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar was a prolific scholar and an influential leader of the Dalit community in India.
    • He played a crucial role in drafting the Indian Constitution and was a strong advocate for the rights of the oppressed and marginalized.
    • Ambedkar's efforts led to significant social reforms, including the abolition of untouchability and the promotion of education and employment opportunities for Dalits.
    • He embraced Buddhism in 1956 along with many of his followers, which marked a significant movement in the Dalit community towards religious and social empowerment.
  • Social Reform Movements in India
    • Social reform movements in India aimed at eradicating social evils and injustices prevalent in society, such as caste discrimination, gender inequality, and child marriage.
    • Prominent social reformers included Raja Ram Mohan Roy, who worked towards the abolition of Sati, and Jyotirao Phule, who fought for the rights of the lower castes and women's education.
    • These movements laid the foundation for a more equitable and just society in India by challenging traditional norms and advocating for progressive changes.
    • The contributions of leaders like BR Ambedkar were instrumental in shaping modern India's social and political landscape.

questions.question: ‘Drain of Wealth’, a critique of the colonial exploitation, was given by which of the following nationalist leaders?
questions.questionHtml: ‘Drain of Wealth’, a critique of the colonial exploitation, was given by which of the following nationalist leaders?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Dadabhai Naoroji.

Key Points

  • Dadabhai Naoroji, also known as the "Grand Old Man of India", was an early Indian political leader, merchant, scholar, and writer.
  • He is best known for his work in the Indian National Congress and his influential economic writings on the drain theory, which criticized British economic policies in India.
  • In his book "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India", he detailed how the British were draining India of its wealth.
  • Naoroji's economic analysis and advocacy laid the groundwork for Indian economic nationalism and inspired future leaders like Mahatma Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru.

Additional Information

  • Drain of Wealth Theory
    • The "Drain of Wealth" theory proposed by Dadabhai Naoroji argued that Britain was systematically transferring Indian wealth to Britain.
    • Naoroji highlighted that a significant portion of India's wealth and resources were being drained to Britain without any adequate economic or material returns to India.
    • This theory was primarily articulated through his writings and speeches, particularly in his seminal work "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India".
  • Indian National Congress (INC)
    • Founded in 1885, the Indian National Congress was one of the first political movements to demand greater autonomy and self-governance for India.
    • Dadabhai Naoroji was one of the founding members and served as the President of the INC three times.
    • The INC played a crucial role in the Indian independence movement, advocating for civil rights, representation, and eventually complete independence from British rule.
  • Economic Nationalism
    • Economic nationalism is a body of policies that emphasize domestic control of the economy, labor, and capital formation, often advocating protectionism and import substitution.
    • Dadabhai Naoroji's critique of British economic policies laid the foundation for economic nationalism in India, influencing the Swadeshi movement and later economic policies post-independence.

questions.question: Khudai Khidmatgars, a non-violent movement among the Pathans was started by _____.
questions.questionHtml: Khudai Khidmatgars, a non-violent movement among the Pathans was started by _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan.

Key Points

  • Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan was a prominent leader in the Indian independence movement, advocating for non-violent resistance against British rule.
  • He founded the Khudai Khidmatgar ("Servants of God") movement in 1929, which was composed primarily of Pashtuns (Pathans) from the North-West Frontier Province.
  • The movement emphasized social reform, education, and the upliftment of the Pashtun community, aligning closely with the principles of Mahatma Gandhi's non-violent resistance.
  • Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan is often referred to as the "Frontier Gandhi" due to his dedication to non-violence and his close association with Mahatma Gandhi.

Additional Information

  • Khudai Khidmatgar Movement
    • The Khudai Khidmatgar, also known as the "Red Shirts", was a non-violent movement founded by Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan in 1929.
    • The movement aimed to promote social and educational reform among the Pashtuns of the North-West Frontier Province (now Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in Pakistan).
    • The Khudai Khidmatgar adopted a uniform of red shirts and practiced non-violent resistance, inspired by the teachings of Mahatma Gandhi.
    • The movement played a significant role in the Indian independence struggle, particularly in mobilizing the Pashtun community against British colonial rule.
  • Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan
    • Born in 1890 in what is now Pakistan, Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan was a towering figure in the Indian independence movement.
    • He was a close associate of Mahatma Gandhi and an ardent advocate of non-violence.
    • He spent much of his life working for the social upliftment and political rights of the Pashtun community.
    • Despite facing repression from both the British authorities and later the Pakistani government, Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan remained committed to his principles of non-violence and social justice.

questions.question: Who founded the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) in Calcutta?

  1. Statistics
  2. Computer science
  3. Mathematics
  4. Operation Research
  5. Information science.

questions.question: Who introduced the 'Doctrine of Lapse'?
questions.questionHtml: Who introduced the 'Doctrine of Lapse'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is " Lord Dalhousie".

Key Points

  • Lord Dalhousie served as Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856.
  • He introduced the passenger trains in railways in 1853, the electric telegraph in 1852, and uniform postage in 1854.
  • He described all three as " Three great engines of social improvement".
  • He has started engineering college in Roorkee.
  • He made his summer capital Shimla.
  • He is the founder of the " Public Works Department" or " PWD" in India.
  • He has also served as " Governor General of Canada" or " Commander- in - chief" in India.

​Important Points

  • Lord Wellesley introduced Subsidiary Alliance by virtue of which the Indian kingdoms lost their sovereignty to the English during 1798.
    • Fourth Anglo Mysore was fought during the governor-generalship of Lord Wellesley.
    • During this war, Tipu Sultan died in the battle of Seringapatam in 1799.
    • Fort William College was started by Lord Wellesley in the year 1800.
  • Lord Canning served as Governor-General of India from 1856 to 1862.
    • He also served as the first Viceroy of India.
    • The Mutiny of 1857, which he was able to suppress successfully,
    • Passing of Indian Councils Act, 1861 which introduced a portfolio system in India.
    • Withdrawal of the “Doctrine of Lapse” was one of the main reasons for the mutiny of 1858.
    • Introduction of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
  • The Vernacular Press Act was passed in 1878 by Viceroy Lord Lytton (1876-1880).

Additional Information

  • The doctrine of lapse was an annexation policy.
  • The policy was applied by the British East India Company until 1859.
  • Under this Doctrine, when the ruler of a protected state died without a natural heir, his state was not to pass to an adopted heir as sanctioned by the age-old tradition of the country.
  •  It was to be annexed to the British dominions unless the adoption had been clearly approved earlier by the British authorities.

questions.question: Who among the following revolutionaries was popularly known as 'Master Da'?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following revolutionaries was popularly known as 'Master Da'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Surya Sen.

Key Points

  • Surya Sen was popularly known as 'Master Da'.
    • Surya Sen, also called Surya Kumar Sen (22 March 1894 – 12 January 1934), was an Indian revolutionary who was influential in the Indian independence movement against British rule in India and is best known for leading the 1930 Chittagong armoury raid.
    • Sen was a school teacher by profession and was popularly known as Master Da.
    • He was influenced by nationalist ideals in 1916 while he was a student of B.A. in Berhampore College (Now Krishnath College).
    • In 1918, he was selected as president of the Indian National Congress's Chittagong branch.

Additional Information

  • Ashfaqulla Khan was an Indian independence activist in the Indian independence movement and co-founder of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association.
  • Batukeshwar Dutt was an Indian socialist revolutionary and independence fighter in the early 1900s.
    • He is best known for having exploded two bombs, along with Bhagat Singh, in the Central Legislative Assembly in New Delhi on 8 April 1929.
  • Ram Prasad Bismil was an Indian revolutionary who participated in the Mainpuri Conspiracy of 1918, and the Kakori Conspiracy of 1925, and fought against British rule in India.
    •  Pandit Ram Prasad Bismil was a freedom fighter who played an active role in India's freedom struggle.

questions.question: Who among the following social reformers founded an educational institution, Hindu Widows Home, in Poona in the year 1896?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following social reformers founded an educational institution, Hindu Widows Home, in Poona in the year 1896?
questions.solution: Dhondo Keshav Karve, an Indian social reformer and educator, founded the Hindu Widows Home in Poona in 1896 to support widows who could not remarry. This institution aimed to provide education and improve the social status of Hindu widows.

questions.question: _______succumbed to injuries inflicted on him during a peaceful demonstration against the Simon Commission.
questions.questionHtml: _______succumbed to injuries inflicted on him during a peaceful demonstration against the Simon Commission.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lala Lajpat Rai.

  • Lala Lajpat Rai died on November 17, 1928 after being seriously injured during a lathi charge by the police.
    • When the Simon Commission visited Lahore on October 30, 1928, Lala Lajpat Rai led the commission's protest in a silent non-violent march, but the police responded with violence.
    • He opposed the commission as not a single Indian was included as a member in it.

Key Points

  • Lala Lajpat Rai was an Indian writer, freedom fighter and politician.
    • He was known as Punjab Kesari.
    • He was one of the three members of the Lal Bal Pal trio.
    • He was also involved in the early activities of Punjab National Bank and Lakshmi Insurance Company in 1894.

Additional Information

  • Bal Gangadhar Tilak endeared as Lokmanya was an Indian nationalist, teacher, and an independence activist.
    • He was one third of the Lal Bal Pal triumvirate.
    • Tilak was the first leader of the Indian independence movement.
    • The British colonial authorities called him "The father of the Indian unrest."
    • He was also conferred with the title of "Lokmanya", which means "accepted by the people as their leader".
    • Mahatma Gandhi called him "The Maker of Modern India". 
  • Bipin Chandra Pal was an Indian nationalist, writer, orator, social reformer and freedom fighter of the Indian independence movement.
    • He was one third of the third of "Lal Bal Pal".
    • Pal was one of the main architects of the Swadeshi movement along with Sri Aurobindo.
  • Gopal Krishna Gokhale was an Indian 'liberal' political leader and a social reformer during the Indian independence movement.
    • Gokhale was a senior leader of the Indian National Congress and the founder of the Servants of India Society.
    • He was the leader of the moderate faction of the Congress Party, which advocated reforms by working with existing government institutions, and was a prominent member of the Poona Association or the Poona Sarvajainik Sabha.

questions.question: Who among the following founded the Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental college?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following founded the Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental college?
questions.solution: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College (now known as Aligarh Muslim University) in 1875 as part of the Aligarh Movement. He believed in promoting modern and scientific education for Muslims and reinterpreting Quran in the light of modern rationalism and science. He also founded the scientific society at Aligarh in 1864.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first Indian to be selected to the British ‘House of Commons’ on a Liberal Party ticket?

questions.solution: The first Indian to be selected to the British House of Commons on a Liberal Party ticket was Dadabhai Naoroji.He was elected as the Member of Parliament (MP) for the constituency of Finsbury Central in the 1892 UK general election.

questions.question: Who founded Shantiniketan near Bolpur on 22 December 1901?
questions.questionHtml: Who founded Shantiniketan near Bolpur on 22 December 1901?
questions.solution: Rabindranath Tagore founded Shantiniketan near Bolpur on 22 December 1901. He was a renowned poet, writer, and philosopher who wrote Gitanjali and founded Vishwa Bharati University. He was awarded the Nobel Prize in 1913 for his work. He also composed the national anthems of India and Bangladesh. In 1919, he renounced the knighthood granted by the British crown after the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre.

questions.question: During the British rule in India, who among the following unfurled the flag of India in Germany in 1907?
questions.questionHtml: During the British rule in India, who among the following unfurled the flag of India in Germany in 1907?
questions.solution: Bhikaji Cama unfurled the flag of India in Germany in 1907, marking a significant moment in the Indian independence movement. The flag she hoisted is considered one of the earliest versions of the Indian national flag.

questions.question: In _________, BR Ambedkar negotiated the Poona Pact with Mahatma Gandhi.
questions.questionHtml: In _________, BR Ambedkar negotiated the Poona Pact with Mahatma Gandhi.
questions.solution: BR Ambedkar negotiated the Poona Pact with Mahatma Gandhi in 1932. In September 1932 gave depressed classes later to be known as Scheduled caste reserved seats in provincial and central legislative councils. The act came into force due to Gandhi Ji's fast unto death.

questions.question: The Prarthana Samaj was established at ______ in the year 1867.
questions.questionHtml: The Prarthana Samaj was established at ______ in the year 1867.
questions.solution: The Prarthana Samaj was established in Bombay in 1867 by Atmaram Panduranga. It aimed to promote theistic worship and social reforms such as opposing the caste system, encouraging widow remarriage, and supporting female education.

questions.question: Which of the following revolutionary freedom fighters was assassinated by Abdul Rashid?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following revolutionary freedom fighters was assassinated by Abdul Rashid?
questions.solution: Swami Shraddhanand, a prominent Indian nationalist and Arya Samaj sannyasi, was assassinated by Abdul Rashid. He played a crucial role in the Hindu reform movements of Sangathan and Shuddhi, and was a strong advocate of women's education and the Hindi language

questions.question: The first President of the All India Trade Union Congress was ____.
questions.questionHtml: The first President of the All India Trade Union Congress was ____.
questions.solution: Lala Lajpat Rai was the first President of the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC), which is the oldest trade union federation in India. AITUC was founded on 31 October 1920 and until 1945, it was the primary trade union organization in India. The main purpose of labor unions is to improve the economic lot of workers by securing better wages and working conditions.

questions.question: Who among the following social reformers founded the Self-Respect Movement?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following social reformers founded the Self-Respect Movement?
questions.solution: Periyar E. V. Ramasamy, who founded the Self Respect Movement, joined the Indian National Congress in 1919 but left in 1925 due to its Brahmin-centric stance. He fought against caste, gender, and Brahminical domination in Tamil Nadu, advocating for human dignity. He led the Justice Party from 1939 and renamed it Dravidar Kazhagam in 1944.

questions.solution: Chittaranjan Das a lawyer from East Bengal, was especially active in the Non-Cooperation movement. Chittaranjan Das is popularly known as 'Deshbandhu'.

questions.question: ___________ offered a scathing criticism of the economic impact of British rule in India through his book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'.
questions.questionHtml: ___________ offered a scathing criticism of the economic impact of British rule in India through his book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'.
questions.solution: Dadabhai Naoroji offered a scathing criticism of the economic impact of British rule in India through his book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'. Dadabhai Naoroji, the “Grand Old Man of India”, was the the first Indian member of the British parliament.

questions.question: On whose advice did Gandhiji spend a year travelling around British India, getting to know the land and its people?
questions.questionHtml: On whose advice did Gandhiji spend a year travelling around British India, getting to know the land and its people?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Gopal Krishna Gokhale.Key Points

  • Gopal Krishna Gokhale was a great social reformer and educationist who provided exemplary leadership to India's freedom movement.
  • Gopal Krishna Gokhale worked towards social empowerment, expansion of education, and struggle for freedom in India for three decades and rejected the use of reactionary or revolutionary ways.
  • Between 1899 and 1902, Gopal Krishna Gokhale was a member of the Bombay Legislative Council followed by work at the Imperial Legislative Council from 1902 to 1915.
  • At the Imperial legislature, Gokhale played a key role in framing the Morley-Minto reforms of 1909.
  • Gopal Krishna Gokhale was associated with the Moderate Group of the Indian National Congress (joined in 1889).
  • Gopal Krishna Gokhale was also associated with the Sarvajanik Sabha journal started by Govind Ranade.
  • In 1908, Gokhale founded the Ranade Institute of Economics.
  • Gopal Krishna Gokhale started an English weekly newspaper, The Hitavada (The people's paper).
  • Gopal Krishna Gokhale became president of INC in 1905 in the Banaras session.
  • Bal Gangadhar Tilak called Gopal Krishna Gokhale the diamond of India.
  • Gokhale was the political guru of Mahatma Gandhi.

Additional Information

  • Bipin Chandra Pal(1858-1932).
    • Bipin Chandra Pal was the main architect of the Swadeshi Movement.
    • He stood against The Partition of Bengal.
    • He was known as the “Father of Revolutionary Thoughts”
    • He worked with Lala Lajpat Rai and Bal Gangadhar Tilak Hence known as “Lal-Bal-Pal.
    • He was also known as Bengal Tiger.
    • He preached the use of Swadeshi and the Boycott of foreign goods to eradicate poverty. 
  • Bal Gangadhar Tilak(1856-1920).
    • ​Bal Gangadhar Tilak raised the slogan, “Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it!”.
    • The word Swarajya was first coined by Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
    • He was also known as Lokmanya Tilak.
    • He established a prominent organization Deccan Education Society to promote modern learning.
    • He also established Fergusson College in Pune.
    • He along with Annie Besant played an important role during Home Rule Movement(1916-18).
    • Kesari and Mahratta were the two newspapers started by; Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
  • Lala Lajpat Rai(1865-1928).
    • He was born in Punjab, Also known by ‘Punjab Kesari’.
    • He was influenced by Swami Dayananda Saraswati and joined the Arya Samaj in Lahore.
    • Along with Bipin Chandra Pal and Bal Gangadhar Tilak, he formed the Lal-Bal-Pal trio of extremist leaders.
    • He Fought against untouchability.
    • Lala Lajpat Rai Founded the Servants of People Society in 1921.
    • Lala Lajpat Rai Founded Arya Gazette.
    • Lala Lajpat Rai founded the Home Rule League of America in 1917 in New York.
  • Mahatma Gandhi(1869-1948).
    • Mahatma Gandhi, by name of Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, (was born on October 2, 1869, in Porbandar, India.
    • Mahatma Gandhi was an Indian lawyer, politician, social activist, and writer who became the leader of the nationalist movement against the British rule of India. 
    • Mahatma Gandhi came to be considered the father of India.
    • Mahatma Gandhi was known for his non-violence protest and was a leading figure in freedom movements.
    • Mahatma Gandhi's important movements, Champaran Satyagraha (1917), Non-Cooperation Movement (1920, Civil-Disobedience Movement (1930), and Quit India Movement (1942).

questions.question: Who among the following social reformers established Satyashodhak Samaj?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following social reformers established Satyashodhak Samaj?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Jyotirao Phule.Key Points

  • Satyashodhak Samaj (Truth-seeker's Society) was a social reform society founded by Jyotirao Phule in Pune, Maharashtra, on 24 September 1873.
  • It espoused a mission of education and increased social rights and political access for underprivileged groups, focused especially on women, Shudras, and Dalits, in Maharashtra.
  • Satya Shodhak Samaj refused to regard the Vedas as sacrosanct, opposed idol worship, denounced the Chaturvarnya System (the caste system), and rejected the need for a Brahman priestly class as educational and religious leaders.
  •  The existence of God was replaced by Nirmik.
  •  Deenbandhu was the name of the mouthpiece of the Satya Shodhak Samaj.

Additional Information

Jyotirao Phule:

  • He was born on 11 April 1827 in Katgun, Satara District in Maharashtra.
  • He belonged to the Mali caste of gardeners.
  • It was in 1848 that he read American political activist and philosopher’s work ‘Rights of Man’, this book influenced his idea of social justice.
  • He is credited with using the word ‘Dalit’ for the depressed classes for the first time.
  • It is a Marathi word meaning ‘broken’ or ‘crushed’.
  • Phule inspired many latter-day leaders including B R Ambedkar.
  • Phule was also the Commissioner of the Poona Municipality from 1876 till 1883.
  • Mahatma Phule passed away in Pune aged 63.

Important Points

  • Some of Mahatma Phule’s published works- 
    • Tritiya Ratna
    • Brahmananche Kasab
    • Powada : Chatrapati Shivajiraje Bhosle Yancha (Life of Shivaji)
    • Manav Mahammand (Muhammad) (Abhang)
    • Gulamgiri
    • Satyashodhak Samajokt Mangalashtakasah Sarva Puja-vidhi
    • Sarvajanic Satya Dharmapustak
    • Shetkaryacha Asud

questions.question: Who was the political guru of Subhash Chandra Bose?
questions.questionHtml: Who was the political guru of Subhash Chandra Bose?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Chittaranjan Das

Key Points

  • Chittaranjan Das was the political mentor of Subhash Chandra Bose.
  • Chittaranjan Das was a prominent leader in the Indian independence movement and an advocate for self-governance.
  • He played a significant role in Bose's early political career and was instrumental in shaping his nationalist ideas.
  • Das founded the Swaraj Party in 1923 along with Motilal Nehru to express the discontent with the policies of the British government.
  • Subhash Chandra Bose admired Das for his dedication to the cause of Indian independence and considered him a guiding force in his own political journey.

Additional Information

  • Subhash Chandra Bose was a prominent leader in the Indian independence movement known for his radical approach and leadership of the Indian National Army (INA).
  • He was a key figure in the struggle against British colonial rule and sought to achieve independence through armed struggle.
  • Bose's famous slogan was "Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom!"
  • He formed the Azad Hind Government in exile during World War II and sought support from Axis powers to fight against the British.
  • Despite his controversial alliances, Bose remains a revered figure in Indian history for his dedication and sacrifices for the nation's independence.
